slides.heading: Apartment Hunting
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Very Hard · Arrays
slides.narration: Let's solve Apartment Hunting, a very hard arrays problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Blocks list which buildings (reqs) they contain.
Choose the block minimising the farthest distance you'd walk to reach any required building.
Precompute nearest distance per req with a left and right sweep.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Blocks list which buildings (reqs) they contain. Choose the block minimising the farthest distance you'd walk to reach any required building. Precompute nearest distance per req with a left and right sweep.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: For each requirement, precompute the distance from every block to its nearest building, with a left and a right sweep.
slides.narration: For each requirement, precompute the distance from every block to its nearest building, with a left and a right sweep.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: For each block, scan all blocks for each req → O(b² · r)
Two sweeps per requirement → O(b · r)
slides.narration: Scanning outward from every block is quadratic. Two linear sweeps per requirement give nearest distances, so the whole thing is blocks times requirements.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 1. For each requirement, sweep left to right and right to left
3. For each block, take the max over requirements
4. Pick the block with the smallest max
slides.narration: Step by step. First, for each requirement, sweep left to right and right to left. Second, store min distances. Third, for each block, take the max over requirements. Fourth, pick the block with the smallest max.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Distance to nearest requirement, per block
slides.narration: For each requirement, two sweeps, left to right and right to left, give every block's distance to the nearest one.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Worst-case per block; minimum at block 3
slides.narration: Each block's score is its farthest requirement. The minimum, 1, is at block 3.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: For each requirement, the forward sweep tracks the last block with it and the backward sweep the next one; each block keeps the min, and worst keeps the max across requirements. Return the index of the smallest worst.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of b times r. Space is O of b times r.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
slides.narration: Use large sentinel distances before the first occurrence.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
slides.narration: Frame it as minimising the maximum distance.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: For each requirement, precompute the distance from every block to its nearest building, with a left and a right sweep.
slides.narration: To recap Apartment Hunting: For each requirement, precompute the distance from every block to its nearest building, with a left and a right sweep. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
